summary: Correction round addressing AUDIT-OPUS-01's two blocking findings (F1, F2) and the remaining fixable findings (F3, F5, F6, F8, F9, F10, F11, package wiring) in ledger/executor-caller.mjs, ledger/fault-matrix.mjs and their test suites. Two findings (F4: one-shot runner invocation handoff protocol; F7: static PID-1 C wrapper) are explicitly de-scoped as larger than this round and recorded as open work, not attempted. Codex (gpt-5.6-sol, high reasoning) implemented; I independently reviewed every changed line and re-ran all verification outside Codex's own sandbox (the sandbox denies a nested spawnSync/FIFO test unrelated to this diff). HEAD unchanged; nothing committed.
findings: F1 (blocking) - FIXED. executor-caller.mjs now tracks killRequested provenance: when the outer-timeout callback's killGroup call succeeds, any subsequent close observation is fed to the fault matrix as rawExit:{kind:'unknown',code:null} instead of the real signal/exit, because a caller-requested kill cannot be distinguished from a natural terminal observation after the fact. The real observed rawExit (e.g. {kind:'signal',code:9}) is still retained and returned to the caller in result.rawExit for evidence/diagnostics; only the fault-matrix input is provenance-adjusted. If killGroup itself throws (kill denied/failed), killRequested stays false and a later natural close still flows through as a genuinely retained main failure -- verified by a new test ('a failed kill request does not hide a later retained natural main failure') showing PROCESS_FAILED/MAIN_EXIT_NONZERO is preserved in that case. fault-matrix.mjs's precedence order was not changed, matching the audit's statement that the matrix itself is not at fault. The test at executor-caller.test.mjs (previously asserting PROCESS_FAILED/MAIN_SIGNAL and titled as a feature) is retitled 'outer timeout retains its close signal but classifies the caller kill as unknown' and now asserts PROCESS_UNKNOWN/3/MAIN_EXIT_UNAVAILABLE while still asserting exactly one killGroup call and result.rawExit still reflecting the real signal.

F2 (blocking) - FIXED. The fault-matrix input constructed in executor-caller.mjs no longer invents stopReturnCode:0, timerCancelReturnCode:0 or timerCancelReceiptPersisted:true, and no longer derives terminalEvidencePersisted/stopReceiptPersisted from 'exit kind known and durable read succeeded'. All four are now honest non-observations: stopReturnCode:null, stopErrorClass:null, stopReceiptPersisted:false, timerCancelReturnCode:null, timerCancelReceiptPersisted:false, terminalEvidencePersisted:false (this caller never performs or observes an exclusive terminal-evidence write with fsync -- that remains the systemd collector's job per spec.md line 68, not this module's). Consequence, stated plainly: PROCESS_SUCCESS is no longer reachable from executor-caller.mjs in this round. Because terminalEvidencePersisted is unconditionally false and the fault matrix's precedence order requires it true before reaching the stop/timer/containment gates, every path through this caller now bottoms out at PROCESS_UNKNOWN (EVIDENCE_WRITE_FAILED, MAIN_EXIT_UNAVAILABLE, or CONTAINMENT_UNRESOLVED depending on the case) or PROCESS_FAILED for a genuinely retained known main failure. This is the correct outcome given what this caller actually observes; no new production code was added to synthesize these facts. fault-matrix.mjs itself remains capable of producing PROCESS_SUCCESS when a different, more complete caller supplies every independently observed success fact -- the pure classifier was not weakened.

F3 - FIXED. containment() in executor-caller.mjs now throws EXECUTOR_DURABLE_RESULT_SCHEMA unless the durable result's schema field is exactly 'moriarty.loan-process-result/1' (the spec's schema, not the previous fixture's 'moriarty.local-financial-integration/1'), and throws EXECUTOR_DURABLE_RESULT_STATUS unless the document's own status field ('PASS'/'FAIL') is consistent with the actually observed rawExit (exit/0 implies PASS; exit-nonzero or signal implies FAIL; anything else is rejected). Both failure modes are treated as an unresolved/failed durable read (resultReadFailed=true), never as containment. The test fixture's schema was corrected to moriarty.loan-process-result/1 throughout, and a new test ('schema-invalid or exit-inconsistent durable results cannot establish containment') exercises both the wrong-schema and status/exit-mismatch cases.

F5 - FIXED. runProverBoundedExecutor now unconditionally requires writeControlRecord to be a function and unconditionally awaits it with no try/catch swallow before spawn; a thrown error always propagates and aborts before any spawn call, regardless of the legacy requireControlRecord flag's value. The flag is still accepted and type-checked for backward compatibility but no longer has any effect on whether the control record must be written or on whether a write failure is swallowed. The two tests that previously asserted PROCESS_SUCCESS with no writer or after a failed write are rewritten ('legacy optional-control flag cannot permit spawn without a writer' / 'legacy optional-control flag cannot swallow a failed control write or spawn') to assert rejection with no spawn call in both cases, matching the pattern of the pre-existing 'required control persistence failure prevents every child spawn' test, which is unchanged.

F6 - FIXED. A second bounded timer (ABANDON_AFTER_KILL_MS, default 1000ms, overridable per-call via the new optional abandonAfterKillMs run option) now starts immediately after the outer-timeout kill attempt. If the child has not closed or errored by the time that second timer fires, the promise is forced to settle with rawExit:{kind:'unknown',code:null} rather than hanging forever. All timers are cleared on every settlement path via a single clearTimers() helper. A new test ('a child that never closes after a failed deadline kill settles at the abandonment bound') proves the promise settles within a bounded wait when the fake child never emits close/error after an (also-failing) kill attempt.

F8 - FIXED, two parts. (1) fault-matrix.mjs gained one new branch, inserted immediately after the knownMainFailure check and before the terminalEvidencePersisted check: an unknown/null rawExit with no higher-precedence disqualifier now classifies as PROCESS_UNKNOWN/3/MAIN_EXIT_UNAVAILABLE (the spec's line-66 code for 'outer kill without a retained terminal observation' or 'collection cutoff with only running observations'), rather than falling through to the unrelated EVIDENCE_WRITE_FAILED. This is additive only; every pre-existing row/precedence test in fault-matrix.test.mjs still passes unchanged, plus one new row test. (2) executor-caller.mjs no longer loads stopErrorClass from the caller's own killGroup error class; stopErrorClass is now always null (per F2), and the kill's own error class is instead surfaced only in diagnostics.killErrorClass for observability, never conflated with the spec's distinct 'failed collector stop' field.

F9 - FIXED. The tautological 'let cleanupCalls=0; ... assert.equal(cleanupCalls,0)' in fault-matrix.test.mjs was deleted; the test's two real assertions (source-purity regex, unresolved-evidence classification) are unchanged and still pass.

F10 - FIXED within the scope this round can honestly cover. executor-caller.mjs now passes an explicit, validated env object to spawn (defaulting to {} when the caller supplies none), never process.env or undefined (which Node treats as full parent inheritance). This does not implement the full MORIARTY_INVOCATION_SOCKET/MORIARTY_INVOCATION_NONCE handoff (that remains F4, out of scope) -- it removes the specific defect named (spawning with zero env keys means silent full inheritance) and gives a real caller a place to put those two variables once the handoff protocol exists. A new run-option field env (flat string-to-string map, validated the same defensive way other plain-object inputs in this file are validated) was added; omitting it defaults to {}, not inheritance. Tests cover both the default {} case and explicit pass-through without merging.

F11 - FIXED. A new test ('child error rejects with the original spawn error') covers the previously untested child.once('error') path. The close handler's synchronous body (including the classifyRawExit call) is now wrapped in try/catch so a malformed (status,signal) pair from an injected fake rejects the returned promise with the classifier's real error message (verified by a new test, 'malformed close payload rejects instead of escaping the promise', asserting rejection with EXECUTOR_RAW_EXIT_SIGNAL) instead of throwing uncaught.

Package wiring - FIXED. package.json's test:ledger script now also runs ledger/prover-lifetime.test.mjs, ledger/executor-caller.test.mjs and ledger/fault-matrix.test.mjs (appended, existing 25-file list unchanged in order); test:executor is retained unchanged as an independently invocable alias. No dependency was added; npm dependency count remains zero.

F4 - DE-SCOPED, recorded as OPEN, NOT implemented. The 'Concrete one-shot runner invocation handoff' requirement (spec.md lines 29-40: AF_UNIX stream socket in a mode-0700 runtime dir, mode-0600 socket, 256-bit nonce, explicit env-only MORIARTY_INVOCATION_SOCKET/MORIARTY_INVOCATION_NONCE pinning that overwrites inherited values, constant-time nonce/authority comparison, socket peer UID check, /proc PID-ancestry verification with retained start ticks, exactly-one-handshake enforcement, a pre-handshake durable invocation-event append with 'failed append yields no handshake', and the EOF-before-setup-refuses/EOF-after-startup-initiates-cleanup semantics) is not present anywhere in this diff and was not attempted this round, per explicit instruction. This corrects the previous round's report, which listed this requirement under 'implemented' while disclosing the omission elsewhere -- that self-assessment was wrong per the audit (its F4) and is now retracted: the requirement is open, not met, not partially met by the argv-delivery test. The seven denial cases in the spec's 'Actual runner-to-script protocol' scenario (forged nonce, wrong authority/reservation, stale store event, different launcher PID, replay, boot mismatch, parent disappearance) remain entirely unexercised and cannot be exercised without the channel.

F7 - DE-SCOPED, recorded as OPEN, NOT implemented. The 'Prover lifetime established before daemon startup' requirement's compiled-artifact half (spec.md lines 100-127: one small import-free static PID-1 executable at plugins/moriarty-dev/scripts/moriarty_dev/prover_lifetime.c, with reproducible build instructions, and offline tests that compile that actual wrapper and drive controlled child programs that exit, hang, fork, change process group and ignore signals, plus parent-death/reap/signal-forwarding behavior) does not exist anywhere in the tree and was not attempted this round. ledger/prover-lifetime.mjs and its test suite were not modified in this correction round; they remain, as the audit correctly characterizes them, a pure JS model of the wrapper's arithmetic and control-record byte format only -- correct and well-tested as a model, but not the compiled executable the spec requires, and not established process-level behavior (fork/process-group/reap/signal-forwarding/parent-death). No attempt was made to misrepresent the .mjs module as satisfying this requirement.
process_success_reachability: PROCESS_SUCCESS is not reachable from executor-caller.mjs (neither runExitRetainingExecutor nor runProverBoundedExecutor) after the F2 fix, in any test in the corrected suite or in principle: terminalEvidencePersisted is unconditionally false because this caller never performs or observes the exclusive fsynced terminal-evidence write the spec assigns to the systemd collector, and fault-matrix.mjs's existing (unchanged) precedence order requires that field true strictly before it will consider the stop/timer/containment gates that stand between a known-good exit and PROCESS_SUCCESS. This is the correct and intended state of this caller in this round, not a regression to be worked around. fault-matrix.mjs itself is untouched in its ability to produce PROCESS_SUCCESS given a complete, honestly-observed input from a future, more complete caller (e.g. one that actually runs the systemd collector/stop/timer machinery described in spec.md lines 74-79).

open_questions: F4 (concrete one-shot runner invocation handoff: AF_UNIX socket, nonce, env pinning, peer UID, PID ancestry, one-shot handshake, pre-handshake durable event, EOF semantics, seven denial cases) is open and unimplemented. It requires a genuinely new module (the socket/handshake layer) which this round's file-scope constraint (no new modules) and explicit instruction both excluded. A follow-on round should either implement it as a new module or the architect should decide whether executor-caller.mjs's current argv-and-clock-only scope is an acceptable, explicitly-labeled partial substitute pending that work.

F7 (static PID-1 C wrapper at plugins/moriarty-dev/scripts/moriarty_dev/prover_lifetime.c, with reproducible build and offline process-level tests) is open and unimplemented. This is a distinct engineering task (C, not JS) outside this file-scope's language and directory boundaries; ledger/prover-lifetime.mjs's pure model remains valid as the arithmetic/byte-format reference the eventual C wrapper should match, but does not substitute for it.

Whether a future caller should synthesize terminalEvidencePersisted/stopReceiptPersisted/timerCancelReceiptPersisted from a real systemd collector integration (per spec.md lines 74-79) is unresolved; this round deliberately leaves PROCESS_SUCCESS unreachable from executor-caller.mjs rather than guessing at that integration's shape.
